run.display_title: refactor(sim): the tick's rules parsed in the crate (spec 39 step 8c-ii)
run.head_commit_message:
feat(sim): the digest as a cargo binary (spec 39 step 8c-xiii) (#686)

* feat(sim): the digest as a cargo binary (spec 39 step 8c-xiii)

`native/bin/breach_digest` plays formation_digest.gd's runs in the crate
with no Godot: each set's runs in the digest's order and by its labels
(`digest::runs`), every tick's record chained with SHA-256 and printed as
the digest prints it, `out=` lines too. CI's `digests` jobs run it after
the Godot digest and fail unless its run lines and `out=` file are the
same.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi5XN6pxL5nz53P7mfo

* feat(sim): BattleTrials as a cargo binary (spec 39 step 8c-xiv) (#687)

8c-xiv split further: the battle trials here; the fatigue, path and sight
trials (8c-xv), scaling_check (8c-xvi) and the benches (8c-xvii) follow.

- src/trials.rs fights BattleTrials' six scenarios on a fresh crate per
  run: the mirrors through Play till fewer than both sides stand, the
  field's through FieldPlay (eight grem builders, as BattleTrials makes
  it) till the kingdom's line breaks; each unit lost counted once; the
  summary and lines as formation_trials.gd prints them.
- src/bin/trials.rs, copied to native/bin/breach_trials by build.sh.
- Play::stands, which both_stand now uses.
- CI's trials job diffs the crate's lines against Godot's: the mirrors
  over 50 runs both ways round, and every scenario over 10.

Outcomes don't change.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi4p5tsXQKAaq18ABgm

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): fatigue trials played in the crate (#688)

FatigueTrials as breach_native::trials::fatigue: a stout wave engages a
holding line, fights it for a set time and retreats; the line's pursuit,
stamina at the turn and tiredness measured as Godot measures them.
breach_trials scenario=fatigue prints formation_trials.gd's lines, and
CI's trials job diffs them against Godot's over 10 runs. Spec 39 step
8c-xv split further: the path and sight trials are 8c-xvi.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2uhgnKKkzsrosdD8o

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): path and sight trials played in the crate (#689)

PathTrials and SightTrials (formation_trials.gd's paths) in the crate
(spec 39 step 8c-xvi): breach_trials scenario=paths [repeats=20] plans
each trip for each walker over the field with the crag, draws the
whole-field ways and feels along SightTrials' wall, printing the same
lines as Godot. Each side times its own searches, so CI's trials job
diffs the two outputs with the timings blanked on both sides.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi4CrbX2o7tmwGUPenu

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): scaling_check timed on the crate's tick (spec 39 step 8c-xvii) (#690)

* feat(native): scaling_check timed on the crate's tick (spec 39 step 8c-xvii)

breach_scaling times the crate's own tick on scaling_check.gd's battles
(FormationBench.clash and, new in the crate, .lanes as Battle::Lanes),
prints its lines and exits 1 on a doubling past the limit. CI's scaling
jobs run it after Godot's on the same runner and diff the untimed
columns. A cargo test holds each stage's set-up equal to Godot's.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi4uaJfy4dLJTMjTmY7

* fix(ci): the crate's scaling check made executable before it runs

The sim-checks scaling jobs have failed on every PR since #690 with
"native/bin/breach_scaling: Permission denied" (exit 126): a
downloaded artifact loses its exec bit. The step now runs chmod +x
first, as the digest's and the trials' steps already do.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2Cf7tsPnWjxmAVjzP

* feat(native): tick_phases timed on the crate's tick (spec 39 step 8c-xviii) (#691)

breach_tick_phases brings tick_phases.gd's battle to its fight in the crate and
times the crate's own tick pass by pass: each pass ends a lap (src/laps.rs),
counted only while the bench times it. Printed as tick_phases.gd prints it, so
the bench workflow runs it (tool=breach_tick_phases) and bench_compare.py reads
it. The set-ups are held to Godot's tick and event counts by a cargo test.
8c-xviii is split further: rout_bench and native_bench's columns are 8c-xix,
spec 38 step 2's series, terrain=mixed and counts 8c-xx.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi1syjMvBE1GZmEPgGf

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): rout_bench and native_bench timed in the crate (spec 39 step 8c-xix) (#692)

breach_rout_bench sets up rout_bench.gd's battle in the crate (many friendly
formations along one lane, the front half routing back through the rear) and
times the rout's pass alone, as FormationRout.step runs it. breach_native_bench
brings FormationBench's clash to its fight and times the crate's tick on one
thread and on the pool, with the bodies' parting and the seek inside it; the
Godot boundary's sync, call and write columns have no crate counterpart. Cargo
tests hold both battles to Godot's events and digest state.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2ApkbYs1VEQnhzjWF

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): tick_phases series=1 timed on the crate's tick (spec 39 step 8c-xx) (#693)

breach_tick_phases takes series=1 and limit=: every tick from contact until
one side no longer stands or limit ticks, with each phase's mean on the lines
bench_compare.py reads, then the tick's and each phase's 95th and 99th
percentiles (nearest rank), worst and worst tick after a "series:" line.
bench_compare.py compares those percentiles' medians when every round has
them. Spec 38 step 2's terrain=mixed and counts are split off as 8c-xxi and
8c-xxii.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2k9DkfrHPCpmmUFt1

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): tick_phases terrain=mixed, the clash across a wood and a ford (spec 39 step 8c-xxi) (#694)

breach_tick_phases and tick_phases.gd take terrain=mixed: FormationBench's
clash on a 128 x 64 ground, its line of advance along y 32, crossing a wood
16 cells deep and then a stream too deep for grems with a 32-cell ford.
The layout is recorded in spec 38. GDScript: FormationBench.mixed and
mixed_ground(). Crate: ground::map::mixed, battles::Battle::Mixed and
phases::Options::mixed. The bin exits 2 for another terrain, or for mixed
with squads above 1.

The crate's battle is held to a Godot probe's on the same ground
(phases::tests::GODOT_MIXED: events over 400 ticks and DigestState.state's
SHA-256 at ticks 130 and 400). It matched first time.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2h89SgVHD8rj3fCum

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): tick_phases counts=1, each pass's changed slots against the living (spec 39 step 8c-xxii) (#695)

breach_tick_phases takes counts=1: after the times, each pass of the tick
in its order, the unit store's slots it changed and the living as it
began, a lap, and the share changed (spec 38 step 2's measure for Q24).

laps::lap now takes the field and shows it to a watcher while
laps::watched runs, its time left out of the next lap. phases::counts
copies the store's columns at each lap and compares every column of
each slot. The bin counts the untimed twin, so timed runs don't change,
and the twin must still end where the timed battle does.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi5Gin9en78UVDebW4w

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(native): snapshot tests cut from the digest's battles (spec 39 step 8d-i) (#696)

A cut is a digest battle's state after a tick (the snapshot's bytes, its
run's label and the squads listed). `cuts::resumed` reads it back into a
Play and steps the next tick, fingerprinting the field and the squads as
each lap ends; `laps::lap` now shows the squads to the watcher too.

Eight cuts from the standard digest's mirrors and clashes, chosen so that
every phase the battles act in changes the state in one, are committed
under native/rust/cuts/ (about 390 KB) and written by
`breach_digest cuts=<dir>`. Cargo tests require each to still be the
battle's state and to step as recorded. 8d is split: the field logs'
cuts, which must carry FieldPlay's state, are 8d-ii.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi54GBMMXTnTmXqUXg1

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(native): cut the field logs for the snapshot tests (spec 39 step 8d-ii) (#697)

* feat(native): carry a field's own state beside the crate's

FieldPlay::carried writes what a field log keeps beside the snapshot (the
squads listed, the definitions coded, the routes' codes, the waves, the
builders' work and reserve, hurry and tending); FieldPlay::carrying sets
the field up from its record again and lays that over it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011AyPi2epF3P2hExj2PS5Uu

* test(native): cut the field logs for the snapshot tests

A cut of a field log carries FieldPlay's own state (<name>.field) and is
stepped with the record's commands for its tick. Three field cuts (field1
at 120, field2 at 229, field3 at 470) cover the pathing, the withdrawal and
the carrying, which leave cuts::UNCHANGED. Closes spec 39 step 8 (8d-ii).
